_about: Hand labels for the race-post relevance threshold (scripts/calibrate_race_post_relevance.py writes app/data/race_post_relevance.json from them). One row per stored production race_coverage_items row on 2026-10-17 that was posting-eligible before that day's fixes: a news item matched on the full_name basis and not a multi-story digest by news_digest.digest_reason. id is the production row id, relevance the stored race_relevance cosine, names_the_race whether the text names the race's state or another of its candidates (CandidateMatcher.names_the_race), not_on_november_ballot whether the race's state has certified November candidates and the matched candidate is not among them (on 2026-10-17), posted whether Civitas published a post from it. about_race is 1 when the story is about the contest for that seat (the campaign, its candidates' campaigning, polls, debates, ads, endorsements, fundraising, nominations and results) and 0 otherwise: a member's official business, a race for another office (a member running for governor), national politics naming the member, or someone else of the same name. No headline or name is stored here.
_why_hand_labels: No source states which race a story is about. The nearest publisher label, a section path such as The Hill's /homenews/campaign/, says a story is about an election, not which one: the candidate's 2028 presidential speculation is filed there too, and most outlets in the feeds file by date only.
_labelled: 2026-10-17, every eligible row (830), by Claude Code (the agent that prepared the fix) reading each headline and feed description against its matched race; not yet reviewed by a person.
